title: Booking System Schema Design
description: Design a reservation schema for resources, time slots, and availability checks

data.text: Booking systems must enforce availability, handle cancellations, and track resource utilization. The schema needs to prevent double-booking while keeping historical records accurate.

data.title: Booking DDL
data.content: Create resources and bookings with time slot tracking and overlap prevention.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE resources (
  resource_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  name VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
  type VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  capacity INT NOT NULL,
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE
);

CREATE TABLE bookings (
  booking_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  resource_id INT NOT NULL,
  user_id INT NOT NULL,
  start_time DATETIME NOT NULL,
  end_time DATETIME NOT NULL,
  status VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'confirmed',
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE booking_slots (
  slot_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  booking_id INT NOT NULL,
  slot_date DATE NOT NULL,
  slot_time TIME NOT NULL,
  is_available BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE
);

data.title: Important
data.text: Use EXCLUDE constraints or application-level locking to prevent overlapping bookings on the same resource.

items.question: How do I prevent double-booking?
items.answer: Use unique exclusion constraints or check for overlaps in application code with serializable isolation.

items.question: Should I store start_time and end_time or use slots?
items.answer: Use both. Store range times on bookings and generate granular slots for availability grids.

items.question: How do I handle time zones?
items.answer: Store all times in UTC and convert to local time only at the presentation layer.

data.title: Summary
points: Use resources and bookings with time ranges
Prevent overlaps with constraints or locking
Store times in UTC for global support
data.takeaway: Booking schemas must enforce non-overlapping reservations while supporting flexible time-range queries.
